---
title: "Financial Inclusion and Credit Impacts on Crop Production in Ghana"
output:
  # officedown (not word_document) so exhibits can sit in landscape sections;
  # word_document has no mechanism for page orientation.
  officedown::rdocx_document:
    reference_docx: reference.docx
    fig_width: 6.3
    fig_height: 4.5
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 2
    toc_float: true
    css: css/tables.css
bibliography: references.bib
# Citation style — set by scripts/run_article.R's CITATION_STYLE, which exports
# ARTICLE_CSL. The fallback below is what a bare knit (RStudio's Knit button,
# no pipeline) uses, so it tracks CITATION_STYLE's default. Files live in csl/:
#   IEEE (numbered):                 csl/ieee.csl               [current]
#   Elsevier Harvard (author-date):  csl/elsevier-harvard.csl
#
# Every citation in sections/ is bracketed (`[@key]`), so both styles render
# without rewriting prose. Two things do NOT follow the switch automatically:
# reference.docx styles the bibliography for hanging-indent author-date, and
# 02_data.Rmd still carries five hand-typed markers "[21], [22], [23], [25],
# [26]" left over from the pre-Harvard draft. Under IEEE those are
# indistinguishable from citeproc's own output while pointing at nothing.
csl: "`r Sys.getenv('ARTICLE_CSL', 'csl/ieee.csl')`"
link-citations: true
---
